summary: Atsuuji Ashikaga worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Doshisha University and under Ryosaburo Sakaki at Kyoto University, later serving at Kyoto University (1930–1962), the Society for Near Eastern Studies in Japan, and Tokai University.
Atsuyoshi Keika is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He held posts as lecturer (attested 1990) and professor (attested 2014) at Otani University.

Atul Chandra Chatterjee worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under Charles Henry Tawney at the University of Calcutta and Presidency University, and later at King's College, Cambridge, before serving in the Indian Civil Service from ~1897 to 1931.

August Blau was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under August Friedrich Pott and Carl Cappeller, earning his Ph.D. from the University of Jena, and worked at Wrocław University Library, Göttingen State and University Library, and Berlin's Humboldt University from 1892.

August Boeckh was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied under Friedrich August Wolf and Friedrich Schleiermacher, and later held academic posts at Heidelberg University (1807–1811) and the Humboldt University of Berlin (1811–1861).
August Clemens Schoener was an Indologist and linguist. Between 1890 and 1894, he pursued theology studies at the University of Munich and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg.

August Conrady worked in sinology, tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg, Jena, Strasbourg, Leipzig, and Würzburg under Julius Jolly. He held posts at Peking University (1903–1904) and the University of Leipzig from 1891 until his professorship.
August Constantin Boltz was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Jena (~1843–1845) and served as a professor at the Prussian Military Academy between 1852 and 1864.

August Dillmann worked in linguistics and religious studies. Educated at Tübingen under Heinrich Ewald, Rudolf von Roth, and August Schleicher, he held professorships at Tübingen, Kiel, Giessen, and the Humboldt University of Berlin / Frederick William University Berlin (1869–1894).

August Ferdinand Naeke was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1805–1810) and later held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1817–1818) and the University of Bonn (~1818–1838).

August Fick was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey, Heinrich Ewald, and Karl Friedrich Hermann at the University of Göttingen (1852–1856). He later held professorships at Göttingen (1876) and the University of Breslau (1888–1891).

August Fischer was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1885–1889) and held posts at the University of Leipzig (~1900–1930) and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (~1904–1914).

August Friedrich Pott was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Karl Otfried Müller, Franz Bopp, and Wilhelm von Humboldt, later serving on the faculty at Berlin (1830–1833) and Halle-Wittenberg (1833–1887).

August Hermann Francke was a scholar in tibetology, linguistics, and history. He studied at Niesky, Moravian Theological College, and Berlin, and held academic posts at the Humboldt University of Berlin from 1922, becoming professor in 1925.

August Hjalmar Edgren worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Uppsala and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, he taught at Yale, Lund, the University of Gothenburg, and served as professor at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln across two periods.

August Johan Bernet Kempers specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Nicolaas Johannes Krom at Leiden University and directed the Dinas Purbakala, the Netherlands Open Air Museum, and taught European ethnology at the University of Amsterdam.

August Leskien was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher, and served as a professor of Slavic philology and comparative linguistics at the University of Leipzig from 1870 to 1915.
August Ludwig von Schlözer worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Uppsala University (~1755–1756) and held a post at the University of Göttingen from ~1769 to 1809.

August Schleicher was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Bonn under Fleischer, Ewald, Ritschl, and Lassen, later serving as professor at Charles University / German University in Prague (1850–1857) and Jena (1857).
August Sundin is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who has been a PhD student at Ghent University (attested 2024–2026).
